text:
maya: Quick follow-up from the granular shard eviction RFC. Observed double-evict + transient read failures in canary when a shard handoff crosses two nodes during a slow network window.
chris: Can you paste the minimal repro or logs?
maya: Repro snippet from canary logs:
```
[evict] shard=granshard-42 -> handoff sent to nodeB
[nodeB] applies evict -> but nodeA times out waiting for ack and re-sends
[nodeB] sees duplicate and evicts again -> clients hit empty-read for a few ms
```
ravi: So nodeB is not de-duplicating idempotent handoffs? We assumed seqno+shard would be unique.
maya: Right. Problem is we don't persist a short-lived idempotency vector for recently processed handoffs; relying solely on in-memory seqno means duplicates across restarts cause trouble.
olivia: Thoughts on fix paths? Options:
• handshake ACK with causal token persisted to small stable cache (fast write)
• include watermark epoch in lease so duplicate applies are no-ops
• keep existing but make client read fallback more tolerant (retries)
chris: ACK+causal token sounds clean but adds a roundtrip on handoff. Concern: extra latency on hot handoffs.
ravi: We can make ACK async: nodeB applies locally, writes token to a tiny replicated memtable, responds ACK; but that still needs a durable write if we want cross-restart safety.
maya: Proposal sketch:
1) Handoff includes handoff_id (UUID) and from_epoch.
2) Receiver applies evict and atomically append handoff_id to an in-memory LRU + write-ahead append in a "stabilizer" segment (batched fsync occasionally).
3) Sender waits for ACK with committed_lsn; on timeout it may retry but receiver de-dupes by handoff_id.
This keeps steady-state latency low since stabilizer fsync is batched. Also bounds disk use.
olivia: Operational questions: how big is stabilizer WAL? Who GC's it?
maya: GC plan: stabilizer acts as circular log per-node, retention window = max(retry-window) + safety_margin (default 5m). GC run by background compaction.
sre-bot: Note: this introduces a new disk artifact; SRE needs alerting for stabilizer growth > 1GB.
chris: Edge: if receiver crashes before WAL persist but after applying evict in-memory, duplicate after restart could reapply -> still double-evict. Need durability at least for quick window.
ravi: Could avoid durable writes by making receiver respond ACK only after write-ahead append; so sender's retry logic is correct. That adds latency but only on first handoff; many handoffs will be local and cheap.
maya: Tradeoffs: (a) zero-durability = cheaper but unsafe across restarts; (b) WAL-on-ack = safe but higher p99 on handoff. I lean WAL-on-ack with batching to amortize.
olivia: For canary we can enable "de-dupe-only-in-memory" to test behavior without disk change.
chris: Can we do client-side fallbacks too? e.g., on empty-read, client retries a second time with prefer-stable-read header to query fallback node.
maya: Yes but that's bandaid; prefer core correctness in handoff.
ravi: Rollout plan suggestion:
- Phase 1: in-memory de-dupe on canary (no fs changes)
- Phase 2: WAL-on-ack in staging with stabilizer GC + SRE alerts
- Phase 3: enable globally + monitor metrics (evict-double-count, empty-read spikes)
maya: Metrics to add: handoff_id_retries, stabilizer_wal_bytes, evict_apply_latency, empty_read_rate
olivia: I'll add dashboard tiles and a small smoke test that simulates delayed ACKs.
chris: I'll open an RFC followup PR with design + perf numbers and the canary config knobs.
maya: Thanks. Owners: chris (PR + rollout), olivia (dash + smoke), ravi (impl plan for stabilizer), maya (coord). Any objections?
ravi: none from me.
olivia: :thumbsup:
chris: :+1:
maya: Updating the RFC doc now and will post a link.
maya: Updated RFC follow-up: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1234#handoff-stabilizer
